title: Decouple consumer processing into stage boundaries and add graceful quiesce for rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Our Redis/Kafka consumer code has accreted synchronous responsibilities across message ingestion, business transformation, retry orchestration, and acknowledgement. This tight coupling makes graceful rolling upgrades, hotspot backpressure handling, and targeted perf optimizations difficult. We've observed retry storms and elevated 95th-percentile latencies during maintenance windows and when tail latencies spike. Goal: Decompose the consumer pipeline into explicit stages (Ingress -> Transform -> Delivery -> Ack) with bounded handoff queues, pluggable retry/admission policies, and a cluster-wide quiesce mode that drains work without dropping messages. This ticket drives the core refactor, dependency upgrades to the redis client, and benchmarks to validate improvements.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Consumers are refactored into modular stages with clear interfaces and bounded handoff queues. 2) Quiesce mode can be signaled to a host (via SSM/consul/console toggle) and drains in-flight batches within a configurable timeout without leaving orphaned inflight messages. 3) Retry orchestration is pluggable and defaults to exponential backoff with jitter; we demonstrate a switch to token-bucket rate-limited retries. 4) Redis client upgraded to latest stable; no regression in connection stability under stress. 5) CI e2e tests cover graceful shutdown/drain, at-least-once semantics, and backpressure scenarios. 6) Performance regression <3% p50 and improved p95 by at least 10% for typical request mixes.
tasks: Design and spec stage boundaries and APIs (ingest/transform/delivery/ack)
Implement bounded handoff queue abstraction with backpressure signals
Introduce QuiesceCoordinator and integrate a host-level signal path
Pluggable retry adapter: default exponential-jitter + optional token-bucket plugin
Upgrade redis client from redis-py v3.6 -> v4.3 and run compatibility tests
Add CI e2e scenarios for rolling upgrade/drain and high-retry storms
Benchmark harness: baseline and post-change p50/p95/p99 under 3 workloads
Rollout plan: canary two clusters, monitor metrics & rollback criteria
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Decouple+consumer+stages+design. Benchmark dashboard (baseline): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/consumers/baseline. Initial spike investigation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/432. Approach trade-offs: 1) Bounded queues add backpressure which can increase upstream latency for bursts; mitigated by adaptive admission and short max queue sizes. 2) Quiesce window must balance draining vs. prolonging maintenance; default 60s with per-cluster override. 3) Redis client upgrade requires re-validation of multi-key LUA scripts and pipelining semantics.

Security (Vikram Patel): No secrets exposed by quiesce signal; verify audit logs for admin toggles
Perf (Sanjay Rao): Add stage-level histograms and a live SLO dashboard before broad rollout
Design (Emily Chen): Prefer explicit interfaces over implicit channel semantics to ease future plugins
risks_mitigation: Risk: Increased upstream latency during backpressure. Mitigation: adaptive admission with short-burst bypass and circuit for high-priority tenants.
Risk: Redis client upgrade introduces API regressions. Mitigation: run multi-region staging with production traffic replay and validate LUA scripts.
Risk: Partial drain leaves duplicate processing. Mitigation: tighten ack window and increase end-to-end test coverage for at-least-once semantics.
qa_plan: Add unit tests for queue boundaries and retry adapter, add integration tests simulating Redis flaps and Kafka rebalance, add chaos tests for quiesce signaled mid-batch. Validate p95/p99 in performance lab and confirm telemetry emits per-stage counts and latencies.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary on low-traffic cluster for 24 hours and validate queue depth, retry rates, and p95. 3) Expand to 30% traffic for 48 hours. 4) Full rollout if no regressions and steady-state metrics within threshold. Rollback: disable feature flag and revert canary hosts to previous binary.
final_notes: This refactor should reduce maintenance-induced retry storms and make future per-stage optimizations safer. Follow-up tickets will convert specific stages to actor-based workers and add tenant-aware admission policies.
